claims.claim_text: The indexed John F. Cady is a high-confidence match to the Burma analyst documented in the Truman Library oral history as serving in OSS from 1943 to 1945.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Research analyst, Office of Strategic Services, 1943-1945
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official oral-history heading and first-person transcript identify the exact name, OSS service dates, Burma specialty, and recruitment chronology.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the exact uncommon full name with middle initial, explicit OSS service, Burma analyst role, and matching 1943 chronology; no private identifier links the sources directly.
claims.temporal_assessment: The oral history dates his OSS service to 1943-1945 and describes the immediately preceding Franklin College role.
claims.match_notes: Box 100 remains necessary to confirm the private identifier and personnel-file linkage, so the identity is not labeled confirmed.

claims.claim_text: John F. Cady's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was Franklin College in Indiana, where he was teaching and serving as dean before his 1943 OSS invitation.
claims.evidence_excerpt: I was teaching at Franklin College in Indiana when World War II started.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Cady says he was teaching and serving as dean at Franklin College before he was invited to Washington to join OSS in 1943.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence exact-name OSS match supported by a first-person federal oral history and the indexed Box 100 row.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate chronology: Franklin College employment precedes and is directly connected to the 1943 OSS invitation.
claims.match_notes: Franklin College is published as employment, not education. Exact start and end dates remain unspecified.

sources.excerpt_override: I was teaching at Franklin College in Indiana when World War II started.

claims.claim_text: Franklin College is also the last documented civilian employer before John F. Cady's OSS service.
claims.evidence_excerpt: I was invited to come to Washington to be a part of the newly organized Office of Strategic Services
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The first-person sequence moves directly from his Franklin College deanship and teaching to the invitation to join OSS.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence exact-name OSS match supported by the direct oral-history chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate sequence with no intervening military or government affiliation described.
claims.match_notes: This is a last civilian employer claim and does not assign an unproven military status to Cady.

claims.temporal_assessment: The Army record dates entry on February 17, 1943; it does not establish the Army-to-OSS transfer date.
claims.match_notes: The full identifier remains private. No namesake biography or postwar employer is attached.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Rolf Cahn is probably the future Santa Fe resident documented as conducting wartime parachute and resistance-support activity in the European theater.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Rolf Cahn-were parachuting behind enemy lines in the European Theater
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A Santa Fe Reporter historical feature names the rare exact-name Rolf Cahn in wartime European clandestine activity and links the account to a 1994 obituary.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable from the rare exact name, wartime chronology, and European clandestine context; the article does not supply the indexed private identifier or a Box 100 link.
claims.temporal_assessment: The evidence concerns wartime activity and does not establish a pre-OSS employer, occupation, or immediate predecessor.
claims.match_notes: The official Army merged file contains no exact private-identifier record, and its documented omissions make that nonmatch inconclusive. The Packard-foundry namesake lead lacks a prewar date and is not published.
